backlog.title: Fast-Path Concurrency Safety Fixes
backlog.description: Fix two concurrency bugs in runLoopFastPath (the FR-M13/FR-M14 file-disjoint fast-path in internal/decompose/decompose.go). BUG-001 (critical): with --edit, N concurrent editors race on the single shared .git/STAGECOACH_EDITMSG file, silently attaching the wrong message to a commit. BUG-002 (major): all messages generate before any publish, so cross-concept duplicate-subject detection is lost — a single run can emit two identical subjects. Both stem from generateMessage containing operations (EditMessage, stale recent-subjects fetch) that are NOT concurrency-safe under the fast-path's N-way goroutine fan-out. The fix extracts generateMessageCore (generation without EditMessage, with seedRejections for cross-concept retry), moves EditMessage to the serial publish loop, and adds an incremental cross-concept dedupe pass in that same serial loop.

milestones.title: Fix concurrent editor race on fast-path (BUG-001)
milestones.description: Eliminate the shared STAGECOACH_EDITMSG race by deferring EditMessage out of the concurrent generateMessage goroutine and performing it in runLoopFastPath's serial publish loop. This serializes the editor (one at a time, in CAS order) while preserving the concurrency win for message generation (the LLM call stays concurrent). Involves extracting generateMessageCore from generateMessage so the fast-path goroutines can generate messages without invoking the interactive editor.

tasks.title: Extract generateMessageCore from generateMessage
tasks.description: Refactor generateMessage (internal/decompose/message.go:70-222) to split the message generation+dedupe logic (steps 1-6, lines 72-209) into a new function generateMessageCore that does NOT call EditMessage. generateMessage becomes a thin wrapper calling generateMessageCore(..., nil) + EditMessage. The new core function also accepts a seedRejections []string parameter that pre-seeds the dedupe loop's rejection list and extends the dedupe check target, for use by BUG-002's cross-concept retry. All existing callers of generateMessage are unchanged.

subtasks.title: Refactor generateMessage into generateMessageCore + wrapper
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/bugfix/001_fb876ae39715/architecture/fix_design.md Part 1 for the full split design. generateMessage (message.go:70-222) currently does 7 steps: (1) RevParseHEAD, (2) system prompt, (3) TreeDiff, (4) messageRecentSubjects → recent, (5) model resolution, (6) generation+dedupe loop (lines 142-209), (7) EditMessage (lines 212-219). The split point is between step 6 and step 7.
2. INPUT: The existing generateMessage function at internal/decompose/message.go:70-222. No external inputs needed — this is a pure internal refactor.
3. LOGIC: Create generateMessageCore(ctx context.Context, deps Deps, treeA, treeB string, seedRejections []string) (string, error) containing steps 1-6 of the current generateMessage, with TWO modifications for seedRejections: (a) initialize the dedupe loop's 'rejected' slice with seedRejections instead of empty (so prompt.BuildUserPayload includes them in the rejection block); (b) build dedupeRecent = append(recent, seedRejections...) and use dedupeRecent in the generate.IsDuplicate check at line 194 instead of 'recent'. Then generateMessage(ctx, deps, treeA, treeB string) (string, error) becomes: msg, err := generateMessageCore(ctx, deps, treeA, treeB, nil); if err != nil { return "", err }; then the EXISTING EditMessage block (lines 212-219) verbatim; return msg, nil. Preserve ALL existing error types and wrapping (RescueError, ErrMessageFailed, ErrEmptyMessage) exactly. The 'recent' variable in generateMessageCore should still be fetched via messageRecentSubjects (NOT merged with seedRejections) for the system prompt building — only the dedupe CHECK uses dedupeRecent.
4. OUTPUT: generateMessageCore returns (string, error) where the string is the generated+deduped commit message (pre-edit). generateMessage returns the same type with EditMessage applied. Existing callers (runLoop at decompose.go:~515, runSingleEscape, runSingleShortcut, chain.go resolveNewCommit) call generateMessage and see NO behavior change.
5. MOCKING: No mocking needed — pure refactor verified by existing tests passing unchanged. The TDD workflow: existing tests in message_test.go (TestGenerateMessage_*) must pass without modification after the refactor.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Add a JSDoc comment on generateMessageCore explaining: it is the concurrent-safe generation core (no EditMessage, no interactive I/O), used by runLoopFastPath's goroutines; seedRejections pre-seeds the dedupe rejection list for cross-concept retry. Update generateMessage's comment to note it now delegates to generateMessageCore.

tasks.title: Move EditMessage to serial publish loop in runLoopFastPath
tasks.description: Change runLoopFastPath (internal/decompose/decompose.go:680-828) so that concurrent goroutines call generateMessageCore (no editor) instead of generateMessage, and EditMessage is applied in the strictly-serial CAS publish loop after receiving each concept's message and before publishCommit. This eliminates the shared-file race because only one EditMessage runs at a time.

subtasks.title: Switch fast-path launch closure to generateMessageCore
subtasks.context_scope:

subtasks.title: Apply EditMessage in the serial publish loop before publishCommit
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/bugfix/001_fb876ae39715/architecture/fix_design.md Part 2. The serial publish loop is at decompose.go:770-828. It receives res := <-ch, handles errors, then calls publishCommit(ctx, deps, res.treeB, prevSHA, res.msg). EditMessage must be inserted BETWEEN error handling and publishCommit. The stagedConcept 'sc' for this iteration provides sc.prevTree and sc.tree (= treeA, treeB for DiffTreeNameStatus). EditMessage's signature is FROZEN: generate.EditMessage(ctx, msg string, cfg config.Config, editCtx generate.EditContext) (string, error).
2. INPUT: res.msg from the goroutine (generateMessageCore output — the generated message without editing). deps.Config.Edit (bool). sc.prevTree and sc.tree from the stagedConcept for this loop iteration.
3. LOGIC: After the existing 'if res.err != nil' error-handling block (decompose.go:~782-798) and BEFORE 'newSHA, err := publishCommit(...)' (decompose.go:~800), insert: if deps.Config.Edit { nameStatus, _ := deps.Git.DiffTreeNameStatus(ctx, sc.prevTree, sc.tree); edited, eErr := generate.EditMessage(ctx, res.msg, deps.Config, generate.EditContext{Git: deps.Git, TreeSHA: sc.tree, NameStatus: nameStatus}); if eErr != nil { drainMsgs(inflight[i+1:]); return commits, nil, eErr }; res.msg = edited }. The error handling for EditMessage matches the current behavior inside generateMessage: ErrEmptyMessage and editor-abort errors are non-rescue hard errors (propagated directly, NOT wrapped in RescueError). drainMsgs(inflight[i+1:]) prevents goroutine leaks, matching the existing error paths.
4. OUTPUT: res.msg is updated to the edited message before publishCommit. The published commit carries the user-edited message.
5. MOCKING: TDD: write a test that calls runLoopFastPath with cfg.Edit=true and GIT_EDITOR=true (no-op editor) on 2+ disjoint concepts; assert each commit's subject matches its concept's generated message. See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/bugfix/001_fb876ae39715/architecture/test_strategy.md BUG-001 section. The stub editor is wired via t.Setenv("GIT_EDITOR", stubtest.BuildEditor(t)) or t.Setenv("GIT_EDITOR", "true") + cfg.Edit=true. Use dcmMessageMatchManifest for concurrency-safe distinct messages per concept.
6. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change (EditMessage is applied at a new call site with the same FROZEN signature).

milestones.title: Restore cross-concept duplicate-subject detection on fast-path (BUG-002)
milestones.description: Add an incremental cross-concept dedupe pass to runLoopFastPath's serial publish loop. After receiving each concept's generated message, check its subject against a growing set of seen subjects (initialized from the pre-run recent subjects, accumulating each accepted sibling's subject). On collision, re-generate via generateMessageCore with seedRejections containing the seen subjects. If re-generation still collides (exhausts retries), enter the rescue path. This restores US7/FR32's no-duplicate-subjects guarantee without sacrificing the concurrency win (generation stays concurrent; only the dedupe check + re-generation is serial).

tasks.title: Add incremental cross-concept dedupe to serial publish loop
tasks.description: In runLoopFastPath's serial publish loop (after receiving each concept's message, before EditMessage and publishCommit), maintain a growing seenSubjects slice. Check each concept's generated subject against it. On collision, re-generate via generateMessageCore with seedRejections=seenSubjects. Handle rescue if re-generation fails. This runs AFTER the BUG-001 fix (EditMessage in serial loop) so the dedupe check operates on the generated (pre-edit) subject, preserving FR-E3's bypass.

subtasks.title: Add seenSubjects tracking and cross-concept dedupe with re-generation/rescue
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/bugfix/001_fb876ae39715/architecture/fix_design.md Part 3 and bug_analysis.md BUG-002 section. The serial publish loop is at decompose.go:770-828. The dedupe check MUST come BEFORE the EditMessage block (P1.M1.T2.S2) so it judges the generated subject (pre-edit), preserving FR-E3's 'edited message bypasses the re-check'. Key insight: concept[i-1] is already published (CAS) in the previous iteration before concept[i]'s collision is detected, so the re-generation's fresh messageRecentSubjects fetch also includes concept[i-1]'s subject — seedRejections is additional safety that tells the LLM upfront which subjects to avoid.
2. INPUT: res.msg from the goroutine (the generated message, post-generateMessageCore). generateMessageCore from P1.M1.T1.S1 (for re-generation). generate.ExtractSubject and generate.IsDuplicate from internal/generate/dedupe.go (FROZEN signatures). messageRecentSubjects from message.go:323.
3. LOGIC: (a) BEFORE the serial publish loop (after the 'if len(staged) == 0' check, before prevSHA := preRunHEAD), initialize: seenSubjects, _ := messageRecentSubjects(ctx, deps.Git, isUnborn). (b) Inside the serial loop, AFTER the res.err error-handling block and BEFORE the EditMessage block (P1.M1.T2.S2), insert the dedupe check: subject := generate.ExtractSubject(res.msg); if generate.IsDuplicate(subject, seenSubjects) { regenerated, regErr := generateMessageCore(ctx, deps, sc.prevTree, sc.tree, seenSubjects); if regErr != nil { handle same as res.err — check for *generate.RescueError (fix ParentSHA=prevSHA, print FormatRescueMulti, drainMsgs, return DecomposeRescueError); otherwise drainMsgs + return hard error }; res.msg = regenerated; subject = generate.ExtractSubject(res.msg); if generate.IsDuplicate(subject, seenSubjects) { drainMsgs(inflight[i+1:]); return commits, nil, &generate.RescueError{Kind: generate.ErrRescue, TreeSHA: sc.tree, ParentSHA: prevSHA, Candidate: res.msg} wrapped in DecomposeRescueError } }; seenSubjects = append(seenSubjects, subject). The re-generation error handling mirrors the existing res.err handler: RescueError → fix ParentSHA to prevSHA (authoritative in the fast-path), print FormatRescueMulti to deps.Out, drainMsgs(inflight[i+1:]), return *DecomposeRescueError. Non-rescue errors → drainMsgs + return.
4. OUTPUT: No two published commits share a subject. Colliding concepts are either re-generated with a distinct subject or rescued (prior commits stand per FR-M12).
5. MOCKING: TDD: write a test that calls runLoopFastPath with 2 disjoint concepts whose message stub emits the same subject (dcmMessageMatchManifest with identical msg for both rules). Assert no two published commits share a subject. See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/bugfix/001_fb876ae39715/architecture/test_strategy.md BUG-002 section. Expected flow: concept 0 published, concept 1 collides → re-generation → stub still returns same subject → rescue. Assert either DecomposeRescueError with 1 commit, or both published with different subjects.
6. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change (internal dedupe logic).

subtasks.title: Test --edit + disjoint fast-path: no cross-contamination
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/bugfix/001_fb876ae39715/architecture/test_strategy.md BUG-001 section. Skeleton: mirror TestRunLoopFastPath_ConcurrentPublish (decompose_test.go:3142) for repo setup + freeze + runLoopFastPath direct call. Edit wiring recipe from TestCommitStaged_EditGate (generate_test.go:836). Use GIT_EDITOR=true (no-op editor) so each concept's generated message passes through EditMessage unchanged — the test then verifies that each concept gets its OWN message, not a sibling's. dcmMessageMatchManifest provides concurrency-safe distinct messages per concept via input-derived match rules.
2. INPUT: runLoopFastPath from internal/decompose/decompose.go (with P1.M1.T2.S2 applied — EditMessage in serial loop). Test helpers: dcmInitRepo, dcmWriteFile, dcmRunGit, dcmHeadSHA, dcmMessageMatchManifest, stubtest.Build, config.Defaults.
3. LOGIC: (a) Create temp repo, seed a base commit (BORN repo). (b) Create 2+ disjoint dirty files (e.g. a.go, b.go) with content changes. (c) g := git.New(repo); baseTree := rev-parse HEAD^{tree}; tStart, _ := g.FreezeWorkingTree(ctx, baseTree); preRunHEAD := dcmHeadSHA. (d) t.Setenv("GIT_EDITOR", "true") — no-op editor preserves each concept's generated message. (e) cfg := config.Defaults(); cfg.Edit = true. (f) messageM := dcmMessageMatchManifest(t, bin, []messageMatchRule{{substr: "a.go", msg: "feat: add a"}, {substr: "b.go", msg: "feat: add b"}}). (g) deps := dcmDepsWithConfig(t, repo, roles, cfg). (h) concepts := []prompt.PlannerCommit{{Title: "c1", Files: []string{"a.go"}}, {Title: "c2", Files: []string{"b.go"}}}. (i) commits, _, err := runLoopFastPath(ctx, deps, concepts, baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD, false). (j) Assert: err == nil; len(commits) == 2; commits[0].Subject == "feat: add a"; commits[1].Subject == "feat: add b"; commits[0].Subject != commits[1].Subject. Optionally verify via dcmGitOut(t, repo, "log", "--format=%s", "-n1", commits[i].SHA).
4. OUTPUT: A passing test TestRunLoopFastPath_EditGate_NoCrossContamination (or similar name) in internal/decompose/.
5. MOCKING: The message stub (cmd/stubagent via dcmMessageMatchManifest) is the only external dependency. The editor is /bin/true (no mock needed). The git repo is a real temp dir.
6. DOCS: none — test-only file, no user-facing surface.

tasks.title: Regression test for BUG-002 (duplicate-subject collision)
tasks.description: Test runLoopFastPath with >=2 disjoint concepts whose message agent emits the same subject. Assert no two published commits share a subject — one concept must be re-generated with a distinct subject or rescued. This test would fail on the pre-fix code (where both concepts pass the stale dedupe check) and passes on the fixed code (where the incremental cross-concept dedupe catches the collision).

subtasks.title: Test fast-path with same-subject collision: no duplicate subjects
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/bugfix/001_fb876ae39715/architecture/test_strategy.md BUG-002 section. dcmMessageMatchManifest is single-response per rule, so the re-generation stub also returns the same subject — the expected outcome is RESCUE for concept 1 (concept 0 published, concept 1 rescued after exhausting retries). If the implementer prefers to test the SUCCESS case (re-generation produces a different subject), they may set cfg.MaxDuplicateRetries=0 to force immediate rescue (simpler), or enhance the stub to be stateful. Either way, the core assertion is: no two published commits share a subject.
2. INPUT: runLoopFastPath from internal/decompose/decompose.go (with P1.M2.T1.S1 applied — cross-concept dedupe). Test helpers: same as BUG-001 test plus dcmMessageMatchManifest with identical msg for both rules.
3. LOGIC: (a) Same repo setup as BUG-001 test (BORN repo, 2 disjoint dirty files a.txt, b.txt). (b) cfg := config.Defaults(); cfg.Edit = false (isolate BUG-002 from BUG-001). (c) messageM := dcmMessageMatchManifest(t, bin, []messageMatchRule{{substr: "a.txt", msg: "chore: update thing"}, {substr: "b.txt", msg: "chore: update thing"}}) — SAME subject for both. (d) concepts := []prompt.PlannerCommit{{Title: "c1", Files: []string{"a.txt"}}, {Title: "c2", Files: []string{"b.txt"}}}. (e) commits, _, err := runLoopFastPath(ctx, deps, concepts, baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD, false). (f) Assert: either (case A) err is *DecomposeRescueError AND len(err.Commits) >= 1 AND no two subjects in err.Commits are equal; OR (case B) err == nil AND len(commits) >= 1 AND no two commits[i].Subject are equal. In both cases, verify via dcmGitOut that git log does not contain the same subject twice.
4. OUTPUT: A passing test TestRunLoopFastPath_DuplicateSubjectDedupe (or similar) in internal/decompose/.
5. MOCKING: Message stub via dcmMessageMatchManifest (same subject for both concepts). Git repo is real temp dir. No editor involved (cfg.Edit=false).
6. DOCS: none — test-only file.

Safe: each goroutine calls generateMessage, which reasons over a tree-to-tree diff (read-only tree reads) and never touches the live .git/index.' LOGIC: Rewrite the comment block at decompose.go ~745-749 to state: (a) goroutines call generateMessageCore (concurrent-safe: read-only tree reads, no EditMessage, no interactive I/O); (b) EditMessage is applied in the serial publish loop below (one editor at a time in CAS order — FR-E4 'serialized publication'); (c) cross-concept dedupe is checked incrementally in the serial publish loop (each concept's subject checked against seenSubjects before publish — restores US7/FR32); (d) the .git/index safety argument still holds (staging sweep is serial). Also update the comment on the serial publish loop (decompose.go ~770) to mention the dedupe check and EditMessage application steps.
